chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who dies and upon him is a debt [of fasting] from the month of Ramadan. Who should pay it off on his behalf? He said: The closest of the people to him. I said: And if the closest of the people to him was a woman? He said: No, except the men.

key_terms.دَيْنٌ: debt (specifically of fasting in this context)

ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for making up the fasting debts of a deceased person, and does gender matter?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific gender restriction in the obligation of Qada al-Siyam (making up fasts) for the deceased, distinguishing it from other debts where women may also be liable. It highlights the juristic consensus in Shia tradition that the physical act of fasting is primarily incumbent upon male heirs, reflecting the distinct legal capacities assigned to men and women in ritual obligations.
